back: Permissions are granted to roles and users are assigned roles, so access follows job function rather than individual grants.

front: Two extensions in the NIST RBAC model?
back: Role hierarchies (senior roles inherit junior ones) and separation of duty (one person cannot hold two conflicting roles, such as create and approve payment).
When access depends on several dimensions, roles multiply: 6 departments x 4 levels x 3 regions = 72 roles, and each new dimension multiplies again.

front: Does Kubernetes RBAC have deny rules?
back: No. It is purely additive: anything not granted by a Role or ClusterRole binding is refused.
Access granted or denied from attributes of the subject, the object and the environment, evaluated against a set of policies.
The policy enforcement point intercepts the request and enforces the answer; the policy decision point evaluates policy and returns allow or deny.

front: When is ReBAC the right model?
back: When permissions follow relationships: sharing, ownership, folders and nested groups, as in Google's Zanzibar or OpenFGA and SpiceDB.

front: Central PDP vs local policy engine?
back: Central: one network hop per check but instant policy changes. Local library or sidecar: sub-millisecond checks, but changes only apply once pushed to every instance.
Every user and program runs with the smallest set of privileges needed for its job (Saltzer and Schroeder, 1975). It limits the blast radius of any bug.
Denied by default; an Allow grants access; an explicit Deny anywhere overrides every Allow.
A handler checks the caller is logged in or has a role, but not that they may access this specific object ID. API1 in the OWASP API Security Top 10 (2023).

front: Three axes for scoping a grant?
back: Actions (s3:GetObject, not s3:*), resources (one ARN, not *), and conditions (network, MFA, time).

front: What does mTLS give two services?
back: Both present certificates, so each authenticates the other, and the link is encrypted. It does not decide what the caller may do.
A SPIFFE ID is a URI naming a workload (spiffe://trust-domain/path). An SVID is the short-lived X.509 certificate or JWT that proves it.
A privileged service tricked into using its authority for a caller who lacks it. Fix: carry and check the end user's identity, not just the calling service's.
A leaked 1-hour certificate is useful for at most an hour with no human action; a leaked static key works until someone notices and rotates it.
